title: VAE: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
hook: Don't just compress data to a point — compress it to a distribution. That gives a smooth latent space you can sample from to generate genuinely new data.
key_points: An encoder maps each input to a distribution in latent space, not a single point.
A decoder reconstructs data from latent samples.
Training balances reconstruction accuracy against keeping the latent space well-structured.
The smooth latent space lets you sample new, plausible data points.
The autoencoder concept behind latent diffusion models.
content_html: Kingma and Welling introduced the variational autoencoder, which learns to compress data into a latent space and reconstruct it — but with a twist that makes the space useful for generation. Instead of mapping each input to a single latent point, the encoder maps it to a probability distribution, yielding a smooth space you can sample from to create new data.
extra_html:
How it works

The encoder outputs the parameters of a distribution (a mean and a spread) for each input. The model draws a sample from that distribution and the decoder tries to reconstruct the original from it. Training optimizes two things at once: reconstructions should be faithful, and the per-input distributions should stay close to a simple reference distribution. That second pressure keeps the latent space continuous and well-organized, so nearby points decode to similar, plausible outputs and you can generate by sampling from the reference distribution.

Why it matters

VAEs gave generative modeling a principled, stable way to learn a structured latent space — a contrast to the adversarial training GANs use. Their outputs can look blurrier than a GAN's, but the well-behaved latent space proved invaluable: latent diffusion models use an autoencoder of this kind to compress images before running diffusion, making modern text-to-image generation tractable.

related.hook: Pit two networks against each other — a forger making fakes and a detective catching them — and the forger gets so good its fakes look real.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

prereqs.hook: A neural net learns by asking, for every weight, 'how much did you contribute to my mistake?' Backprop answers all of them at once.
